leader.name: Mikhail Volkov
leader.title: General Secretary
leader.biography: General Secretary of the All-Union Communist Party since 1924. Volkov has built a command economy around heavy industry and a party apparatus that reaches into every enterprise, and he treats the coming European crisis as an opportunity to secure the western frontier.

traits.name: Suspicious of the West
traits.description: Diplomatic relations with capitalist powers drift down.

parties.name: All-Union Communist Party
parties.description: The only legal party. Its apparatus controls the state, the army and the press.

parties.name: Left Socialist Revolutionaries
parties.description: A remnant of the revolutionary coalition, tolerated as a rural faction.

parties.name: Constitutional Democrats
parties.description: Exiled and underground; influence limited to émigré circles.

parties.name: Monarchist Union
parties.description: Scattered legitimist networks with no open organisation inside the country.

advisors.name: Andrei Orlov
advisors.description: Head of the party control commission. His approval is required for any senior industrial appointment.

advisors.name: Natalia Lebedeva
advisors.description: A trade union organiser and advocate of expanding consumer goods, popular with the factory committees.

advisors.name: Marshal Boris Yegorov
advisors.description: A staff officer of the old school who insists on thorough mobilisation plans before any frontier adventure.

advisors.name: Viktor Gusev
advisors.description: Runs the foreign intelligence directorate; his network in Tokyo has been reporting on the Far East since 1932.

advisors.name: Prof. Ivan Samoilov
advisors.description: The leading advocate of successive-echelon operations and a critic of the cavalry establishment.

modifiers.name: Five Year Plan
modifiers.description: Production targets are set by the planning commissariat, down to the individual blast furnace.

modifiers.name: Frontier Security Zone
modifiers.description: Fortified districts along the western approaches, with the population organised for civil defence.

modifiers.name: Transport Bottleneck
modifiers.description: The rail net cannot carry both the industrial plan and the army's supply requirements. One of them will be cut.

decisions.name: Second Trans-Siberian Track
decisions.description: Double-track the eastern trunk line so that industry behind the Urals can be supplied without priority conflicts.

decisions.name: Technical Cadre Drive
decisions.description: Promote engineers and skilled machinists into supervisory positions, bypassing party seniority where necessary.

decisions.name: Reorganise the Mechanised Corps
decisions.description: Break up the oversized tank brigades into corps built around independent tank and motor rifle formations.

decisions.name: Frontier Guarantees
decisions.description: Offer security guarantees to the western border states in exchange for transit rights.

decisions.name: Consumer Goods Allocation
decisions.description: Divert a share of light industry to clothing, furniture and household goods to ease pressure in the cities.

agency.name: Foreign Intelligence Directorate
agency.description: A network of resident stations from Tokyo to New York, with a large and well-funded cipher section.
